newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba plans to step up foreign business.
newsitem.headline: Veba plans to step up foreign business.

text.p: Utility Veba AG, fresh from announcing a plan to buy a stake in German chemicals and metals frim Degussa AG, plans to beef up investment abroad, Chairman Ulrich Hartmann said on Thursday
Speaking at Veba's shareholder meeting, Hartmann said Veba over the next five years planned to invest overseas some 12.4 billion marks, or 40 percent of its total investment budget.
The Chairman said he expected the investment to help sales double over the next six to eight years to 50 percent of total turnover.
Hartmann also said he expected Veba's planned stake in Degussa to leave the firm better positioned in the chemicals business and that profits this year will climb from the year before.
Veba said on Wednesday it had agreed to buy 36.4 percent of chemicals and metals firm Degussa, paying 2.9 billion marks or 86.80 marks per share.
Hartmann said there are no plans to increase that stake. "We will only pay as much as is needed to reach our goal," Hartmann said.
Shareholders said they agreed with Hartmann's decision to take the Degussa stake.
Hartmann described the telecommunications market, in which Veba is entering, as "very difficult" and that it faced higher start up costs in the first quarter of 1997 than the year before.
But he added he still expected Veba's telecommunication's operation to turn a profit by 2001/2002.
